gloss: to improve; to make better; to reform

definitions.gloss: to improve; to make better; to reform
definitions.explanation: To change something for the better, addressing problems or deficiencies. Used for both tangible things (processes, conditions) and abstract things (relationships, situations). Central to Japanese business philosophy.

examples.japanese: {生活|せいかつ}{習慣|しゅうかん}を{改善|かいぜん}する。
{労働|ろうどう}{環境|かんきょう}を{改善|かいぜん}するために{会議|かいぎ}を{開|ひら}いた。
examples.english: We held a meeting to improve the working environment.

examples.japanese: {食事|しょくじ}と{運動|うんどう}で{体調|たいちょう}が{大|おお}きく{改善|かいぜん}した。
examples.english: My physical condition improved greatly through diet and exercise.

examples.japanese: この{問題|もんだい}を{改善|かいぜん}しなければ、お{客|きゃく}さんの{満足度|まんぞくど}は{上|あ}がらない。
examples.english: If we don't improve this problem, customer satisfaction won't increase.

notes:
One of the most well-known Japanese business concepts internationally. The noun {改善|かいぜん} (kaizen) refers to continuous, incremental improvement and is widely used as a loanword in English business contexts, particularly in manufacturing and lean management.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {業務|ぎょうむ}{改善|かいぜん}: operational improvement
- {体質|たいしつ}{改善|かいぜん}: constitutional improvement
- {環境|かんきょう}{改善|かいぜん}: environmental improvement
- {改善|かいぜん}{策|さく}: improvement measure
- {改善|かいぜん}{点|てん}: point of improvement

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {直|なお}す: to fix — corrects something broken rather than making something better
- {向上|こうじょう}する: to improve — emphasizes raising quality or level upward
- {是正|ぜせい}する: to correct — fixing something wrong or unjust, more formal
